record.paper_title: Open questions for strongly interacting Fermi gases with zero-range interactions
record.context_brief: Zero-range stability domain and Efimov thresholds
record.original_question: For a three-dimensional two-component Fermi gas with N↑ fermions in one internal state and N↓ fermions in the other, interacting only through zero-range Wigner-Bethe-Peierls s-wave ↑↓ contact conditions at unitarity, determine the full stability domain as a function of the mass ratio m↑/m↓. In particular, for systems (N↑,1) with one ↓ impurity, does the known sequence of Efimov-effect thresholds for N↑ = 2, 3, and 4 continue to N↑ = 5, 6, and higher, and what are the critical mass ratios beyond which the zero-range Hamiltonian is no longer bounded below?

evidence.quote: we conclude that the gas with ( N↑, N↓) fermions is stable for a zero-range ↑↓ interaction, and that the Hamiltonian of the Wigner-Bethe-Peierls model is self-adjoint and bounded from below, if and only if the scaling exponents are all real

We note that the successive critical mass ratios get closer and closer together; mathematically, however, we don’t know whether this sequence continues (is there an Efimov effect for (5,1) bodies? for (6,1) bodies? etc.).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a three-dimensional system of N = N↑ + N↓ non-relativistic fermions in two internal (spin) states, with N↑ particles of mass m↑ in state ↑ and N↓ particles of mass m↓ in state ↓. Identical-spin fermions do not interact, while opposite-spin pairs interact only via the Wigner–Bethe–Peierls zero-range s-wave contact condition at unitarity: for every ↑↓ pair (i,j), as their separation r_{ij} → 0 (other coordinates fixed), the wavefunction satisfies

   ψ ∼ (1/r_{ij}) · A({other coordinates})  (infinite scattering length),

and ψ obeys the free Schrödinger equation away from these contact hyperplanes. The Hamiltonian H is defined as the natural self-adjoint extension determined by these boundary conditions, when such an extension exists and is bounded below.

(a) Determine, as a function of the mass ratio α = m↑/m↓, the full stability domain — i.e. the set of α ∈ (0,∞) for which, for given (N↑, N↓), H admits a self-adjoint realization that is bounded from below (equivalently, all relevant scaling exponents arising in the hyperangular Efimov-type analysis are real).

(b) In the impurity sector N↓ = 1, it is known that there is a critical mass ratio α_c(N↑) such that for α > α_c(N↑) an Efimov effect occurs (the Hamiltonian fails to be bounded below in the zero-range model) for N↑ = 2, 3, 4. Decide whether this sequence of Efimov thresholds continues for N↑ = 5, 6, and beyond: that is, for each N↑ ≥ 5, does there exist a finite critical mass ratio α_c(N↑) ∈ (0,∞) beyond which the zero-range Hamiltonian is unbounded from below, and if so determine α_c(N↑)?
artifact.category_tag: Efimov effect in zero-range Fermi gases
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the Efimov effect persists for (N↑,1) zero-range fermionic systems beyond N↑ = 4 appears to remain open. Numerical investigations of the (5+1) system have found no evidence of a six-body Efimov state up to mass ratios M/m ≤ 12, but no proof exists either of existence or non-existence of a critical mass ratio for N↑ ≥ 5, and the full stability domain at arbitrary (N↑,N↓) is not known.

status_evidence.title: Efimov physics implications at p-wave fermionic unitarity
status_evidence.snippet: For three fermions of mass M and a distinguishable particle of mass m, a four-body Efimov effect exists in 13.384 < M/m < 13.607.
status_evidence.claim: The (3+1) Efimov regime is established, but no analogous result is reported for (N↑,1) with N↑ ≥ 5.

status_evidence.title: Four-body Efimov effect (arXiv:1006.4720)
status_evidence.snippet: In the (5+1) system, no sign of a 6-body Efimov state was found in the mass ratios explored up to M/m ≤ 12.
status_evidence.claim: Numerics in the (5+1) sector have not detected an Efimov threshold, but the question is not resolved analytically.
